As the garment of the sky

 human forms] ‘Venice which was once a tyrant, is now the next worst thing, a slave . . . I had no
conception of the excess to which avarice, cowardice, superstition, ignorance, passionless lust, & all the
inexpressible brutalities which degrade human nature could be carried, until I had lived a few days among
the Venetians’ (S. to Peacock, 8 October 1818, L ii 43).
 the Celtic Anarch] Austria. ‘Celtic’ corresponded to mod. ‘Teutonic’; all tyranny was lawless, so all

paragraphs.source_en:
The MS of these lines on Byron is bound into a copy of 1819 at Yale University (Tinker 1897,
Tinker Collection, Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library). S. sent them to his publisher for inser-
tion into Mary S.’s transcript of the poem, perhaps in consequence of Peacock’s (lost) comments on Childe
Harold iv to which S. replied on 17 or 18 December 1818 (L ii 57–8).
 hearthless] Deprived of inhabitants (127) and spiritual life (105–10).
 the sky] Yale MS; thy sky 1819, 1839, eds. A printer’s dittography from line 168.
